/kind bug

What this PR does / why we need it:
the cluster-info's jws-token didn't update until we update configmap again or restart controller-manager.

Fixes #109233

thanks for checking @enj 

> the reason this occurs is because the controller has no resync interval combined with a sync loop that ignores errors.

oddly, users started reporting this only in recent versions.

> If we wanted to remove the lack of a resync interval (which I would not recommend), you could do something like (this would cause a re-run of the loop every 12 hours on default config):

in kubeadm joining nodes would retry the signature validation for a minute.
12h would be a long time.

> The better solution is to not ignore errors. The controller should simply keep retrying forever with an exponential backoff.

+1. errors should be retried.

issue_context.title: failed to verify JWS signature of received cluster info object, can't trust this API Server
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

we usually find kubeadm join has the problem:
failed to verify JWS signature of received cluster info object, can't trust this API Server
or
could not find a JWS signature in the cluster-info ConfigMap for token ID
when we update cluster-info or bootstrap-token, the controller-manager didn't update the cluster-info.data.jws-token.


### What did you expect to happen?

kubeadm join:
Cluster info signature and contents are valid and TLS certificate validates against pinned roots, will use API Server

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

pkg/controller/bootstrap:

func (e *Signer) serviceConfigMapQueue() {
	key, quit := e.syncQueue.Get()
	if quit {
		return
	}
	defer e.syncQueue.Done(key)

	e.signConfigMap()     // if fail, we need requeue
}

// return err and try again
func (e *Signer) updateConfigMap(cm *v1.ConfigMap) {
	_, err := e.client.CoreV1().ConfigMaps(cm.Namespace).Update(context.TODO(), cm, metav1.UpdateOptions{})
	if err != nil && !apierrors.IsConflict(err) && !apierrors.IsNotFound(err) {
		klog.V(3).Infof("Error updating ConfigMap: %v", err)
	}
}

### Anything else we need to know?

found in 1.20.x, 1.22.x and 1.24.x.

### Kubernetes version

1.20.x
1.22.x
1.24.x

### Cloud provider

<details>
any where
</details>


/sig cluster-lifecycle
/triage needs-information

I saw a few users reporting this on slack recently.
We are not seeing this in the kubeadm e2e tests.
JWS are always populated and valid.

> How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

You seem to show source code, but what are the actual reproduction steps?
Any logs from controller manager?

> /sig cluster-lifecycle /triage needs-information
> 
> I saw a few users reporting this on slack recently. We are not seeing this in the kubeadm e2e tests. JWS are always populated and valid.
> 
> > How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?
> 
> You seem to show source code, but what are the actual reproduction steps? Any logs from controller manager?

the two case we have saw：
1、could not find a JWS signature in the cluster-info ConfigMap
Accoring to the apiserver log, can find the kube-public/cluster-info have been changed by the operator, but can not find controller-manager update kube-public/cluster-info. What's more there are nothing log about controller-manager change this configmap until we restart controller-manager then it recover. After restart, there are have log about this configmap on apiserver and controller-manager.
（Our operation program will modify the number of apiserver replicas from 4 to 2 and from 2 to 4, and will regenerate kube-public/cluster-info, about 3 times a day. Only find problem one time. ）

2、failed to verify JWS signature of received cluster info object, can't trust this API Server 
Looking at the logs of the last month, I did not find that the logs about the kube-public/cluster-info configmap and the kube-system/bootstrap-token secret in apiserver and controller-manager.
We restart the controller-manager to recover the problem, and the apiserver and controller-manager have logs about this configmap, also the jws-token-<token id> have been changed by controller-manager.

> 1、could not find a JWS signature in the cluster-info ConfigMap
Accoring to the apiserver log, can find the kube-public/cluster-info have been changed by the operator, but can not find controller-manager update kube-public/cluster-info. What's more there are nothing log about controller-manager change this configmap until we restart controller-manager then it recover. After restart, there are have log about this configmap on apiserver and controller-manager.

you could try adding --v=10 (or a smaller number) to the components, restart them and try to see if they will show more info when the error happens.

> （Our operation program will modify the number of apiserver replicas from 4 to 2 and from 2 to 4, and will regenerate kube-public/cluster-info, about 3 times a day. Only find problem one time. ）

can you explain why are you doing this?
this sounds strange to me, apiserver replicas in a kubeadm setup are recommended to be an odd number (1,3,5) if you are using stacked etcd:
https://etcd.io/docs/v3.3/faq/#why-an-odd-number-of-cluster-members
https://kubernetes.io/docs/setup/production-environment/tools/kubeadm/ha-topology/

> 2、failed to verify JWS signature of received cluster info object, can't trust this API Server
Looking at the logs of the last month, I did not find that the logs about the kube-public/cluster-info configmap and the kube-system/bootstrap-token secret in apiserver and controller-manager.
We restart the controller-manager to recover the problem, and the apiserver and controller-manager have logs about this configmap, also the jws-token- have been changed by controller-manager.

as a speculation, i think it can happen if there are temporary connectivity issues between the components.

in kubeadm, the contents of the config map are validated here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cde45fb161c5a4bfa7cfe45dfd814f6cc95433f7/cmd/kubeadm/app/discovery/token/token.go#L81
(and the code below it)

i don't think there is a kubeadm bug here.
perhaps kubeadm or the KCM have insufficient tolerance for "certain" conditions, but i would like to understand more about the problem. you need to catch the problem and see why the config map is not updated properly (for example).

it's important to note that we run a lot of CI / e2e tests that use `kubeadm join` with tokens:
https://k8s-testgrid.appspot.com/sig-cluster-lifecycle-kubeadm
only few a few of these test jobs don't use tokens and we have not seen these problems.

Ideally actions against the config map should eventually result in a config map that has the desired state (reconciliation). So the code should be in the lines of - get cm, check if update is needed, update or exit, repeat. If that is not how it works, maybe there are bugs...I don't think it should retry on API calls.

Would you like to help us by working on the fix (PR)?
We are in code freeze for 1.24, currently through. 

Also we might want to add e2e test for this in:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/e2e/lifecycle/bootstrap

> Ideally actions against the config map should eventually result in a config map that has the desired state (reconciliation). So the code should be in the lines of - get cm, check if update is needed, update or exit, repeat. If that is not how it works, maybe there are bugs...I don't think it should retry on API calls.
> 
> Would you like to help us by working on the fix (PR)? We are in code freeze for 1.24, currently through.
> 
> Also we might want to add e2e test for this in: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/e2e/lifecycle/bootstrap

now we add monitor to verify jws-token, and find some k8s cluster have the problem. then we change config map or restart controller manager can fix it. so i think it need retry or requeue to be reconciled

@neolit123 
we find jws-token verify fail, until we change configmap to cause controller work, then jws-token change right.
```bash
kubectl -n kube-public get cm cluster-info -o yaml | grep jws

// do not change kubeconfig, just remove one char in jws-token
kubectl -n kube-public edit cm cluster-info 

kubectl -n kube-public get cm cluster-info -o yaml | grep jws
// two jws-token unequal
```
i think controller manager retry to update configmap can fix this problem.
but there may have any other factor cause this problem. it may be good to run an e2e test, but some online clusters have incorrect jws-tokens that cause kubeadm join to fail. this is a sporadic problem and can only be found when executing kubeadm join, our logs are not kept for so long .

The problem here is that we still have no explanation on why it happens and
how to reproduce it...It seems that the reconciliation logic is not ideal.

If you'd like to send a PR fix I can help reviewing it. We can then work on
an e2e test.
